title: Core Complexity vs. Core Count Trade-off
decision: Chose eight simple, single-issue, in-order cores rather than fewer complex, superscalar, out-of-order cores.
alternatives_or_rejected: Complex superscalar out-of-order cores, which were traditional for high-end server processors.
rationale: Out-of-order and superscalar designs consume disproportionate power and die area for diminishing single-thread returns, limiting the number of cores and overall thread-level throughput.
outcome: Successfully integrated eight full cores within the power and area budget, maximizing throughput for highly parallel workloads.
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly names 'superscalar out-of-order' as the rejected alternative or just implies it by contrasting with traditional high-performance designs.

title: Number of Threads per Core and Multithreading Style
decision: Implemented four hardware threads per core using fine-grained, cycle-by-cycle interleaved multithreading.
alternatives_or_rejected: Simultaneous multithreading (SMT) or coarse-grained multithreading (switching only on long stalls).
rationale: Four threads are sufficient to hide L1 cache miss latencies in a short in-order pipeline, and fine-grained interleaving avoids the complex, power-hungry issue logic required for SMT.
outcome: Achieved high pipeline utilization and 32-way multithreading across the chip with a very simple, low-power core design.
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly contrasts 4 threads with SMT (Simultaneous Multithreading) or just discusses fine-grained multithreading.

title: Floating Point Unit Sharing
decision: Implemented a single shared Floating Point Unit for the entire 8-core chip, rather than dedicating an FPU to each core.
alternatives_or_rejected: Dedicating one FPU to each of the eight cores.
rationale: Commercial server workloads (the target for Niagara) exhibit very low floating-point utilization, so dedicating FPUs to every core would waste significant die area and power.
outcome: Saved substantial area and power, which was reallocated to more cores and threads, while still providing FP capability when needed.
weakest_point: The exact page number or whether they explicitly state 'wasted die area' versus just 'commercial workloads have low FP usage'.

title: L2 Cache Interconnect and Bandwidth
decision: Connected the eight cores to a shared, banked L2 cache using a high-bandwidth crossbar switch.
alternatives_or_rejected: A traditional shared bus for L2 cache access.
rationale: A shared bus would become a severe bandwidth bottleneck and limit scalability with 8 cores and 32 threads; a crossbar provides non-blocking, high-bandwidth access to the L2 banks.
outcome: Sustained the high memory bandwidth necessary to prevent starvation and feed 32 concurrent hardware threads.
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly uses the word 'crossbar' for the L2 interconnect or describes it as a switch/network.

title: Target Workload and Power Optimization Philosophy
decision: Optimized the microarchitecture strictly for throughput of commercial, highly-multithreaded server workloads rather than single-thread performance.
alternatives_or_rejected: Optimizing for single-thread performance or standard SPEC integer benchmarks.
rationale: Server workloads exhibit high thread-level parallelism and are often memory-bound; optimizing for single-thread performance wastes power on features that do not improve overall system throughput.
outcome: Created a highly power-efficient, throughput-oriented processor architecture that challenged the prevailing high-frequency, single-thread design paradigm.
weakest_point: The exact phrasing of the workload justification and whether SPEC benchmarks are explicitly dismissed in the text.
